issue.title: Set SASE_CLIENT in sase-nvim and sase-telegram so Footprint records editor and chat hits

task_type_fields.proposal:
Footprint's CLI recorder (src/sase/footprint/_actor.py) classifies a process as actor=human with via=editor when `SASE_CLIENT=nvim`, and via=chat when `SASE_CLIENT=telegram`. No first-party client sets the variable yet. Every `sase` subprocess that sase-nvim (completion, commands) or sase-telegram (chat-driven commands) spawns therefore records as human/cli, or as unknown when it has no TTY. Its editor and chat usage disappears into the CLI counts, and the plan's `editor`/`chat` via values never appear.

Proposal: set `SASE_CLIENT=nvim` in sase-nvim's environment for every `sase` subprocess it spawns, and `SASE_CLIENT=telegram` in sase-telegram's. Only add the variable to the child env; never overwrite an existing agent marker. Add one test per repo that asserts the spawned env carries the value. docs/reference/environment-variables.md in sase already documents SASE_CLIENT.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: This was proposed by Footprint closeout phase sase-1p1.13 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #2), as the plan required. The change lives in the linked sase-nvim and sase-telegram repos, which epic sase-1p1 never touched; its scope was the sase recorder that reads SASE_CLIENT.

issue.creation_reason: Footprint's recorder already maps SASE_CLIENT to via=editor/chat, but no first-party client sets it, so editor and chat usage is misattributed to plain CLI.
